questions.question: Define freedom of expression / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Define freedom of expression
  • Freedom of expression is the fundamental human right to hold opinions without
  • interference and to seek, receive, and impart information and ideas through any media regardless of
  • frontiers. This right encompasses both verbal and non-verbal forms of communication, allowing
  • individuals to engage in public discourse and critique.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Define a)Misinformation b)Disinformation c)Mal-information / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Define a)Misinformation b)Disinformation c)Mal-information
  • a) Misinformation is false or inaccurate information, often spread unintentionally, while b)
  • Disinformation is false information deliberately created and shared to cause harm or deceive. c) Mal-
  • information is genuine information, not false, but used out of context to inflict harm on a person,
  • organization, or country.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: What is generative AI content? / [CO1, CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• What is generative AI content?
  • Generative AI content is any form of media, such as text, images, video, or audio, that is
  • created, altered, or synthesized by artificial intelligence models. These models learn patterns from
  • vast datasets to produce novel and realistic outputs in response to user prompts.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Outline the steps you would take to conduct a successful interview with a public figure / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Outline the steps you would take to conduct a successful interview with a public figure
  • General answer - To conduct a successful interview with a public figure, you should first
  • conduct thorough research on their background and current activities to formulate relevant, probing
  • questions. Then, establish a clear interview objective and listen actively to the subject's responses,
  • adapting your follow-up questions to delve deeper into key topics.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Identify the key aspects that should be noted when covering parliament and legislature / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Identify the key aspects that should be noted when covering parliament and legislature
  • When covering parliament and legislature, key aspects to note include the context and
  • purpose of debates and voting, focusing on the potential impact of new legislation and policies on
  • the public. You must also observe the power dynamics and political maneuvering between different
  • parties and key figures to provide an insightful analysis beyond mere procedural reporting.
  • Awareness about the parliamentary procedures and privileges are essential to avoid contempt
  • proceedings.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Discuss the importance of asking open-ended questions during an interview / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the importance of asking open-ended questions during an interview
  • Asking open-ended questions is important during an interview because they encourage the
  • interviewee to elaborate beyond a simple "yes" or "no," yielding richer, more detailed, and
  • spontaneous responses. This approach allows the conversation to uncover unexpected insights,
  • personal reflections, and deeper context, ultimately enhancing the quality of the story.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain why descriptive language is important in feature news stories and how it enhances storytelling. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain why descriptive language is important in feature news stories and how it
  • enhances storytelling
  • Descriptive language is important in feature news stories because it uses sensory details to
  • create vivid mental images and emotional resonance for the reader. This enhancement turns simple
  • reporting into engaging storytelling, drawing the audience into the narrative and making the
  • characters and settings feel real.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Discuss the importance of writing effective leads in a news story / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the importance of writing effective leads in a news story
  • Writing effective leads is crucial because the opening sentence or paragraph must
  • immediately hook the reader and summarize the most vital information of the news story. A strong
  • lead accurately reflects the main point while compelling the audience to continue reading by
  • establishing the story's relevance and urgency.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Why interpretative reporting is essential in political journalism. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Why interpretative reporting is essential in political journalism.
  • Interpretative reporting is essential in political journalism because it goes beyond simply
  • stating facts to explain why political events are happening and what their long-term consequences
  • might be. This type of reporting provides necessary context and analysis, helping the public
  • understand the complexities of policy and political decision-making.

questions.question: Argue whether new media has improved or hindered the quality of journalism. Use specific examples to justify your position. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Argue whether new media has improved or hindered the quality of journalism. Use
  • specific examples to justify your position.
  • General answer - New media has arguably improved the quality of journalism by
  • democratizing news dissemination and fostering greater accountability through increased speed and
  • citizen reporting. For example, social media allows journalists to quickly fact-check and disseminate
  • real-time updates, although this speed also necessitates strict editorial oversight to maintain
  • accuracy.

questions.question: Explain how pacing can impact the viewer's experience in a stand-alone episode. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how pacing can impact the viewer's experience in a stand-alone episode.
  • Pacing significantly impacts the viewer's experience in a stand-alone episode by controlling
  • the rhythm and emotional intensity of the narrative. A fast pace can create excitement and suspense,
  • while a slow pace can build atmosphere, allow for character development, and deepen the
  • emotional impact of key moments.

questions.question: Classify the types of news based on geographical location using relevant examples. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Classify the types of news based on geographical location using relevant examples.
  • News can be broadly classified by geographical scope into local, national, and international
  • news, each focusing on events within a specific boundary. Local news, such as a story about a new
  • town council ordinance, focuses on community affairs, while national news covers issues affecting an
  • entire country, like a presidential election. International news reports on significant events occurring
  • globally, such as treaty negotiations between multiple countries.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Analyze the legal challenges presented by AI-generated media (audio, video, images) that realistically depict non-existent events. / [CO1, CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Analyze the legal challenges presented by AI-generated media (audio, video, images) that
  • realistically depict non-existent events.
  • General answer - AI-generated media depicting non-existent events presents significant legal
  • challenges, primarily concerning defamation, copyright, and the right of publicity. If this media falsely
  • portrays a person in a negative light, it can lead to defamation lawsuits and, if a likeness is used
  • without permission, may violate their right of publicity. Furthermore, the use of existing copyrighted
  • works to train AI models and generate new content raises complex issues regarding fair use and
  • intellectual property infringement.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Describe how you would prepare to cover an important political speech of a national leader / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• . Describe how you would prepare to cover an important political speech of a national
  • leader
  • To cover an important political speech, I would first conduct thorough research on the
  • leader's past statements, current policy positions, and the context surrounding the speech to
  • anticipate key themes. During the speech, I would actively listen for major announcements, shifts in
  • tone, or quotes that summarize the speech's main message, while also observing the audience's
  • reaction. Finally, I would immediately begin analyzing the speech's significance and its potential
  • political impact to frame my reporting accurately.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Assess the influence of travel reporting in promoting tourism on local economies. / [CO3] [2x15 =30]
questions.solution_html:
• Assess the influence of travel reporting in promoting tourism on local economies.
  • General answer - Travel reporting exerts a strong influence on promoting tourism by
  • generating curiosity and authentic interest in destinations, directly translating to increased visitor
  • numbers. When journalists highlight unique cultural experiences, local businesses, and sustainable
  • practices, they can help direct tourism spending to local economies rather than just large chains. This
  • exposure can be vital for developing regions, supporting jobs, and funding the preservation of
  • natural and historical sites.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
